headline: Multi-cohort transcriptomics prioritizes candidate genes in immune-mediated disease
label: Transcriptomic Candidate Gene Prioritization
summary: Multi-cohort transcriptomic and single-cell designs now routinely pair machine learning with Mendelian randomization to nominate candidate genes.
synthesis: The common thread is transcriptome-scale prioritization of candidate genes and cell states, typically integrating public cohorts, single-cell RNA sequencing and machine learning. In sepsis, an elastic net 12-gene signature and scRNA-seq identify mitochondrial dysfunction genes, and TYMP is proposed as a candidate protective marker in CD4+ T cells. The same logic extends to reproductive and cervical disease: maternal T cells are identified as the key population in repeated pregnancy loss, and Mendelian randomization of cis-eQTL and pQTL data prioritizes LTA, EIF2AK2 and SPAG1 in cervical carcinogenesis. Cross-cohort DNA methylation and transcriptomic integration prioritizes TP53INP1 in pediatric HAdV-7 sepsis. Methodological work contributes benchmarking of multi-omics integration tools on respiratory datasets, a Shiny-based single-cell atlas for murine lung injury, and locked nasal and blood host-response modules validated across external cohorts.
